reviews.review:
It's a tough choice between Yes/No because the game is not too bad development-wise. However, it's a "death by 1000 papercuts" situation.

The name says "Tycoon" but there is very little tycoon mechanic. You can upgrade items to get more money for food/drink/lodging but that's about it. On Day 3 in game, some customers started to show lower satisfaction (yellow face). Why? Who knows! You can't see what they want and what they don't like. In fact, there are no useful reports in the game at all. You have no idea what drives the revenue or cost exactly and don't know how to improve it. Luckily, it's hard to go bankrupt but again, this ain't no "tycoon".

The tutorial ends abruptly leaving many things unexplained. By the time you get the hang of it through trial and error, there are architectural-level mistakes made. The rooms are only built in same-size "blocks" and you can't change them or move them (even though there is a Move button, it actually only works on items, not whole room blocks).

The events pop up way too early and are inappropriate for the game level. (Maybe don't con a player into paying for an event that improves something they don't even have.) Text is rather confusing. E.g. there is an event which reduces "cost" but cost of what? That turns out to be just the price of building the items. The fortuneteller events promise a "reward" but then you complete the quest and it just disappears. What did I get? Who knows.

But the notifications about the kitchen are the worse. They go like this: [whack!]"Emily is waiting on food producer!". Uh... what? I have multiple ovens, the cook is busy, what is the problem? And notifications disappear before you can read them. No signs on the "food producer" (is this a cook? or an oven?), no information which food customers are waiting for, nothing.

I was expecting this to be like Winkeltje or Tavern Master (both fantastic games) with a hotel vibe, but it has so much less to offer. No story, no trading, very weak decoration aspect. There is nothing to manage even. It's really just an idle game that gets repetitive and boring very fast. I don't think it's worth the price in the current shape, sorry.
